payload.claim: `time.sleep(_RETRY_PAUSE_S)` is called directly through the module attribute rather than taken as an injected `sleep` parameter. This repository has an established, explicit convention against exactly this: `saffron/watch.py`'s `follow()` takes `sleep: Callable[[float], bool] = _sleep_and_continue` 'injected rather than reaching `time.sleep` directly, so a test can drive this loop to a deterministic end without waiting on a real clock' (saffron/watch.py:178, :191-192), `saffron/batch.py:417` likewise takes `sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep`, and `tests/test_batch.py`'s `_raise_on_real_sleep` helper exists specifically to catch 'a build that calls `time.sleep` by its module attribute, rather than the injected `sleep` keyword' (tests/test_batch.py:295-304). `prepare_worktree` could take the same keyword with a `time.sleep` default without changing any of the three callers the spec forbids touching, and the test's only recourse here is to monkeypatch `worktree.time.sleep` directly — the module-attribute pattern the rest of the codebase treats as a defect shape, and nothing stops a future test on this path from forgetting to patch it and sleeping 60 real seconds.
